cells.tense: You're in the middle of it with the questions still open, and that's working.
cells.ask: Name one want out loud today and let that be the whole act.
cells.core:
There's a want on you and you're still asking what it is. You don't close over it to look sure, you keep turning it over, and the pull stays clear because you do. Questions aren't what's between you and the thing you're moving toward. They're how you're finding it.

What you're doing already serves it. The test is letting the answer out of the private room where you keep holding it. Say one want in plain words to someone who can hear it, without moving anything off it first, and notice that it survives being spoken. That's the invitation — take it or don't, and the want is still there either way.
cells.sheetLine: You ask your way toward it, and the asking is working.
cells.verb: learning what you already carry, by asking
cells.place: the pull toward the light you want to move toward

cells.tense: You're already living past this moment, braced against an answer that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Write down how you'd begin one thing, then leave the reply side blank.
cells.core:
You're trying to get to the end of a thing you're still inside. The questions stopped being a way in and became something to produce answers with, and a day that was open in the morning is closed tight by the afternoon. The pull toward the light doesn't need you ahead of it.

Intent runs in an order — a want, then straight steps, then what follows. When that order holds, you move on what you actually want instead of hedging it. Take one thing that matters and write down only the first line, how you'd begin it, that's all. Leave the reply side blank. What you keep from grabbing is what isn't yours yet, and what you get is the thing found rather than forced.

cells.tense: You're still at a threshold that's already behind you, and you haven't stepped past it.
cells.ask: One hour with no notes: go somewhere new and look at something you haven't seen.
cells.core:
The pull is still there and the asking has gone quiet. A want shows up and you file it before you look at it, or you let it pass as someone else's project. The questions that would find it don't get asked, so the want stays a rumor and the light stays a rumor too.

What still works is the picturing — no plan, no point, letting a scene play with no job attached. Watch something new and let wonder do what discipline won't. That's how the current comes back, and it's taken today — an hour with no notes is what brings the charge to the place it's been missing. What you get is the want as something you're allowed to see, not something you owe an answer to.
cells.sheetLine: The pull is there. The asking went quiet.

cells.tense: You're steering by something in yourself and telling yourself the pull is doing the steering.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once: the pull being followed is mine.
cells.core:
You call it the pull deciding. But the reading is yours — you're the one who feels when something points and when it doesn't. You've been treating your own read as something that arrives on its own, so it doesn't get claimed and doesn't get questioned.

Fairness does the smaller thing here, not the grander one. Give and take without tallying, what's right in the moment you're in rather than a standing policy. Say one sentence about the pull being followed — that it's yours — and let it stand. What you get is the sense that the point came from you and can be tested by you, which is the difference between steering and drifting.

attempts.check: The place and the record know only that the person feels pulled toward something they want and that they start from not-knowing; they don't say what the pull is toward or how long it's been misheard, so any specifics would be invented. A reader could fairly say the pull is already clear to them and it's the acting that's stuck, which the ask survives because noticing a pull is useful either way. The phrase 'someone else's project' could still be too pointed if no one else is in the picture; the reader can drop it or say it plainly as what they see. The sentence that was serving me rather than them was the Too Much line about producing answers, so I replaced it with the plain physical shape of the day.
